caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 227 of 1962.
lawyer:
Aminul Huq ----- For the Appellant.
Rabia Bhuiyan ----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Rakhal Chandra Sarkar ----- Appellant.
Vs.
Benode Haldar and ors ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 8. Mr. Aminul Huq the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant has contended that the Lower Appellate Court did not apply its mind to Exbt. 1 to 4 and also to Exbts. A. B. C. which from the basis of the case and upon which the Trial Court has given a finding as to possession in favour of the plaintiff, and that the Lower Appellate Court has erred in law in not considering issues Nos. 2 to 4 and thereby has failed to comply with the provision of Order 20 Rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure. According to the learned Advocate, the judgment of the Court of Appeal below is a diffused one and there is no separate finding or decision upon those issues. He has further contended that there is no positive finding by the Court of Appeal below as to who grew the paddy. His submission is, therefore; that judgment of the Lower Appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal. In this connection the learned Advocate has referred to the rulings reported in AIR 1963 All. 194 in the case of Ganga Singh and other VS. Sontosh Kumar and another; AIR 1962 (S.C.) 1314 (V. 49C 175) in the case of Sir Chunilal Vs. Mehta & Sons Ltd. Vs. Century Spinning and Manufacturing Co. Ltd. 10 D.L.R. 1 Privy Council in the case of K. M. Perera Vs. H. G. Martin Dias; 65 C. L.J. 270 Privy Council in the case of Pir Ahsanullah Shah Vs. Pir Ziauddin Shah; 27 C.W.N. 749 Privy Council in the case of Mohammad Solaiman VS. Kumar Birendra Chandra Singh & others 21 D.L.R. (S.C.) 448 in the case of Madan Gopal & others. Vs. Maran Bepari & ors 21 D.L.R. Dacca 838 in the case of Mahmuda Khatun Vs. Abu Sayed; 21 D.L.R. Dacca 977 in the case of Tamijur Rahman Vs. Md. Altafur Rahman and ors; A.I.R. 1948 Mad. 488 in the case of Kalabasti Veeramma Vs, Pratti Pati Lakshmayya and others and A.I.R. 1947 Patna 334 in the case of Rambijaya Prasad Singh Vs. Sukar Ahir.
